findings.title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, unrelated to the annotation deadlock fix
findings.body: The ticker interval in CleanUpService.Run is changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. Nothing in the PR description or the annotation changes calls for this. It makes every cleanup job (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, short URLs, query history) run ten times as often, which raises DB load on every instance. It looks like a leftover debugging change and should be reverted or justified separately.

findings.title: Routine cleanup progress is logged at Error level, including full ID lists, on every batch
findings.body: CleanAnnotations logs 'Annotations to clean by time' (and the matching 'by count', 'Tags to clean', and 'cleaned ...' messages in the other cleanup paths) with r.log.Error. These are normal successful operations, so they pollute error logs and can trigger error alerting. Each line also includes the full list of up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize IDs, which can be tens of thousands of values per batch, and the 'err' field is always nil on these lines. These should be Debug (or Info) messages, and the ID list should not be logged at that size.

findings.title: Quadratic string building of ID list for SQLite delete
findings.body: In deleteByIDs, the SQLite path builds the IDs list with values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) inside a loop. Each iteration copies the whole accumulated string, so building a list of N IDs costs O(N^2) bytes copied. With the batch size allowed to reach 32767 (as in the new 40003-annotation test), this copies gigabytes of data per batch and runs on every cleanup cycle. Use strings.Builder or strconv.AppendInt to build the list in linear time.
